findings.title: Registered metric-alert handler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertFire` still registers `MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, but this class now inherits abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` without implementing `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Accessing `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector of this type calls `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` and raises `TypeError` instead of preserving the prior no-op behavior. Either provide a concrete implementation or do not register/use this handler until it is implemented.

findings.title: Evaluate docstring still documents the old list return contract
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` now returns a dictionary keyed by `DetectorGroupKey`, but its docstring says it "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". This is the public subclassing contract for detector implementations, so the stale documentation can cause new handlers to implement the previous list-based API and fail when `process_detectors` calls `.values()`.

findings.title: Multi-group occurrence test does not validate the value passed to the hook
findings.body: The packet supplies `group_2` with value `10`, but the expected occurrence is constructed with value `6`; additionally, the mock occurrence builder ignores its `value` argument. Consequently this test passes even if `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the wrong group value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`, which is the key new hook contract for producing occurrence-specific payloads. Make the mock output/assertions depend on `value` and expect `10` for `group_2`.
